es: Interpretar la gramática comprimida de los titulares (presente por pasado, to + verbo por futuro, participio sin be) y expandirla a una frase completa.

teaching.en: Headlines drop articles and the verb be, so «Councillors vote to close town pool» really means that the councillors voted to close it.
teaching.es: Los titulares omiten artículos y el verbo be, así que «Councillors vote to close town pool» significa en realidad que los concejales votaron por cerrarla.
teaching.explanationEs: El presente de un titular suele contar un hecho ya ocurrido: vote = voted.
segments: Headlines drop articles and the verb be, so «Councillors vote to close
town pool» really means that the councillors voted to close it.
teaching.audioText: Headlines drop articles and the verb be, so «Councillors vote to close town pool» really means that the councillors voted to close it.

teaching.en: The present tense also reports recent news: «Bus fare hike hits commuters» tells us that a rise in the fare has already affected people.
teaching.es: El presente también cuenta noticias recientes: «Bus fare hike hits commuters» nos dice que una subida de la tarifa ya ha afectado a la gente.
teaching.explanationEs: Hike = subida brusca de precios; hits está en presente pero equivale a has hit.
segments: The present tense also reports recent news: «Bus fare hike hits commuters»
tells us that a rise in the fare has already affected people.
teaching.audioText: The present tense also reports recent news: «Bus fare hike hits commuters» tells us that a rise in the fare has already affected people.

teaching.en: Another headline says «School strike to start on Monday», which means that the strike is going to start then and has not happened yet.
teaching.es: Otro titular dice «School strike to start on Monday», lo que significa que la huelga va a empezar entonces y todavía no ha ocurrido.
teaching.explanationEs: Sustantivo + to + verbo = is going to / is due to; todavía no ha ocurrido.
segments: Another headline says «School strike to start on Monday», which means that
the strike is going to start then and has not happened yet.
teaching.audioText: Another headline says «School strike to start on Monday», which means that the strike is going to start then and has not happened yet.

teaching.en: Short verbs such as probe, pledge and halt save space: «Mayor pledges to halt library cuts» packs a whole promise into five words.
teaching.es: Verbos cortos como probe, pledge y halt ahorran espacio: «Mayor pledges to halt library cuts» condensa una promesa entera en cinco palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Probe = investigar, pledge = prometer y halt = detener: verbos de una sílaba muy frecuentes en titulares.
segments: Short verbs such as probe, pledge and halt save space: «Mayor pledges
to halt library cuts» packs a whole promise into five words.
teaching.audioText: Short verbs such as probe, pledge and halt save space: «Mayor pledges to halt library cuts» packs a whole promise into five words.

teaching.en: A bid is an attempt, so «Bid to save the old cinema fails» tells us that the attempt to rescue it has failed.
teaching.es: Un bid es un intento, así que «Bid to save the old cinema fails» nos dice que el intento de salvarlo ha fracasado.
teaching.explanationEs: Bid + to + verbo = intento de hacer algo; el verbo final indica el resultado.
segments: A bid is an attempt, so «Bid to save the old cinema
fails» tells us that the attempt to rescue it has failed.
teaching.audioText: A bid is an attempt, so «Bid to save the old cinema fails» tells us that the attempt to rescue it has failed.

teaching.en: «The pool is expected to reopen in May» and «the cost is reportedly high» give us information without naming a source.
teaching.es: «The pool is expected to reopen in May» y «the cost is reportedly high» nos dan información sin nombrar la fuente.
teaching.explanationEs: Is expected to y reportedly son fórmulas impersonales: el dato no está confirmado por una fuente concreta.

prompt.es: Elige la frase completa que expresa el titular de este artículo.

choices.text: The councillors vote every Tuesday to close the town pool.
The councillors will vote on Tuesday to close the town pool.
The councillors voted on Tuesday to close the town pool.

feedback.es: La decisión ya se tomó el martes por la noche: el presente del titular equivale a un pasado, no a una costumbre ni a un futuro.

hint.es: Fíjate en que el artículo dice que la decisión ya se tomó.

origin.text: Headline in the local paper: «Councillors vote to close town pool». The article begins: «The decision, taken late on Tuesday night, will affect two hundred swimmers.»

prompt.es: Completa: «La huelga escolar va a empezar el lunes.»

feedback.es: To + verbo en un titular apunta al futuro: la huelga todavía no ha empezado.

hint.es: El verbo be y to rodean la palabra que falta: expresa un plan futuro.

origin.text: The headline says: School strike to start on Monday. The full sentence is: The school strike is ___ to start on Monday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La policía investiga la causa del incendio.»

answer.text: The police are investigating the cause of the fire

feedback.es: El verbo corto probe equivale a are investigating; la frase completa recupera the y el auxiliar are.

hint.es: Recupera the delante de police y el auxiliar are.

prompt.es: Escucha los titulares y elige qué ha ocurrido ya y qué queda por ocurrir.

choices.text: The cinema attempt has failed, but the strike has not started.
Both the cinema attempt and the strike have already happened.
The strike has started, but the cinema attempt is still going on.

feedback.es: «Fails» cuenta un resultado ya conocido, mientras que «to start» apunta al futuro: la huelga empezará el lunes.

origin.audio: Here are the headlines. Bid to save the old cinema fails. School strike to start on Monday. Mayor unveils plan to slash library costs. The pool is expected to reopen in May, and the repair bill is reportedly very high. That was the news.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se dice que el coste es alto, pero nadie cita la fuente.»

feedback.es: Reportedly indica que el dato circula sin confirmación de una fuente concreta.

origin.text: The newspaper says that the repair cost is ___ high, but nobody has named the source of the figure.

prompt.es: Lee el titular y la línea inferior. ¿Qué da a entender sobre la promesa?

choices.text: That critics praise the mayor for acting so quickly.
That critics doubt the pledge can repair the damage already done.
That the mayor admits the two closures were a mistake.

feedback.es: «Too late» y «have already closed» muestran que los críticos dudan de que la promesa deshaga el daño ya hecho.

origin.text: Headline: Mayor pledges to halt library cuts. Below it: Critics say the move comes too late, as two libraries have already closed.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige el titular que la resume mejor.

choices.text: Night bus cut fails as councillors pledge to strike
Councillors to vote on night bus cut after drivers strike
Councillors vote to cut night bus as drivers pledge to strike

feedback.es: Los concejales ya votaron (presente = pasado) y los conductores han prometido huelga (pledge to strike); las otras versiones alteran quién hace qué y cuándo.

origin.audio: Tonight's top story is about the night bus. Councillors voted on Tuesday to cut the service, which will end in March. The savings are reportedly worth two hundred thousand euros, but the council has not published the figures. Drivers have pledged to strike if the plan goes ahead, and a bid to delay the decision failed last week. Residents who work late say that they will have no other way home, while the mayor insists that the money is needed for schools.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué dato no está confirmado por una fuente.

choices.text: The amount of the savings for the council.
The date on which the service will end.
The vote that took place last Tuesday.

feedback.es: La cifra del ahorro es «reportedly worth» y el ayuntamiento no ha publicado los datos: es lo único que carece de fuente.

prompt.es: Completa: «El intento de reabrir la vieja estación ha fracasado.»

feedback.es: El presente fails del titular equivale a has failed: un resultado ya conocido que se cuenta como noticia.

origin.text: The headline says: Bid to reopen the old station fails. The full sentence is: The attempt to reopen the old station has ___.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué certeza hay sobre la aprobación del plan?

choices.text: It is certain, since the council has promised to approve it.
It is likely, but it has not happened yet.
It is unlikely, because the drivers oppose the plan.

feedback.es: «Is expected to approve … next week» anuncia algo probable y futuro: todavía no hay aprobación.

origin.text: Bus fare hike hits commuters, say drivers. The council is expected to approve the plan next week, and the plan is reportedly worth two million euros.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La alcaldesa ha prometido detener los recortes de la biblioteca.»

answer.text: The mayor has promised to stop the library cuts

feedback.es: Pledges to halt del titular se expande con el auxiliar has, el participio promised y el artículo the.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la expansión fiel de este titular?

choices.text: The library cuts will be halted once a strike takes place.
The library cuts halted a strike that was taking place.
The library cuts have been halted after a strike.

feedback.es: El participio del titular equivale a una pasiva sin be: los recortes se han detenido tras la huelga; las otras opciones cambian el tiempo o la voz.

origin.text: Headline: Library cuts halted after strike.
